claims.text: The studied alloy is nominally Nb25Ta25Ti25V25, with a measured composition of Nb23.8Ta25.5Ti24.9V25.8.
The NbTaTiV alloy was arc melted and homogenized at 1200°C for 3 days.
The processed NbTaTiV alloy exhibits a single BCC solid-solution phase.
The single BCC phase of the standard NbTaTiV alloy remains stable up to 900°C.
Severe lattice distortion caused by the random distribution of multiple elements makes dislocation cores deviate from their neutral planes.
Lattice distortion produces wavy edge-dislocation cores or wavy dislocation lines in refractory BCC high-entropy alloys.
The wavy configuration of edge dislocations limits their mobility.
The NbTaTiV alloy has a nearly elastically isotropic response at room temperature.
The room-temperature elastic isotropy is caused by reduced mobility of wavy edge dislocations.
Elastic anisotropy in NbTaTiV gradually increases at elevated temperatures.
The persistence of lattice distortion governs the elevated-temperature elastic-anisotropy behavior through its effect on dislocations.
The yield strength of the standard NbTaTiV alloy decreases as temperature rises from room temperature to 900°C.
The yield strength of NbTaTiV decreases from 1064 MPa at room temperature to 595 MPa at 900°C.
The high-distortion alloy will have a higher room-temperature yield strength than a conventional BCC alloy or a modified low-distortion HEA.
Reducing atomic-size mismatch will reduce lattice distortion while preserving a similar composition and BCC structure.
Reducing lattice distortion will increase dislocation mobility.
The increased dislocation mobility in the modified alloy will lead to lower yield strength and more conventional dislocation behavior.
In situ neutron diffraction and compression testing can be performed at room temperature, 500°C, 700°C, and 900°C at a strain rate of 1×10^-4 s^-1.
The NbTaTiV alloy has a room-temperature Zener anisotropy ratio of approximately 1.2 and a universal anisotropy index of 0.
